anomalies.observed: On the Motion Sensing / CAN BUS tile, U31 pin 2 is labeled NET0059. On the CM4 tile, the same global label NET0059 is attached to Module1 pin 128, which is CAM0_D0_N. This connects the input of the ESTOP_OUT buffer to the CM4 camera data line.
anomalies.expected: The e-stop path should be driven by the e-stop sink/ESTOP_OUT circuitry (or a fixed logic level for an open-drain sink), not by an unrelated camera interface signal. The specification describes an e-stop loop with sink buffers feeding ESTOP_OUT, not a camera-data-driven e-stop output.

evidence.quote: U31 pin 2 label: NET0059 (Motion Sensing / CAN BUS tile)
Module1 pin 128: CAM0_D0_N, net label NET0059 (CM4 tile)
an e-stop loop with multiple sink points ... gated through single non-inverting buffers ... feeding an ESTOP_OUT signal shared with the CAN connectors J2/J13

anomalies.impact: The e-stop output would be controlled by, or loaded by, the CM4 camera data line instead of the intended e-stop loop. This can prevent reliable e-stop assertion and corrupt camera data if the camera interface is used.

parsed.summary: The drawing shows a likely anomaly: the ESTOP_OUT buffer U31 input is tied to the CM4 camera data net NET0059 (CAM0_D0_N), merging an unrelated camera signal into the e-stop path instead of using the specified e-stop sink circuitry.
